title: Tucker Carlson and Historical Revisionism in British Debate
seoTitle: Tucker Carlson and Historical Revisionism in British.
subtitle: The American host questions World War II facts alongside Jacob Rees-Mogg
excerpt: In a televised debate, Tucker Carlson claims Hitler's invasion of Poland was due to border issues, while Jacob Rees-Mogg corrects his assertions.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Tucker Carlson sparked controversy by claiming that Adolf Hitler's invasion of Poland was merely a reaction to the Treaty of Versailles. In a recent debate with Sir Jacob Rees-Mogg, the American presenter questioned widely recognized historical facts.

Carlson's Claims About the Outbreak of War

During the broadcast, Carlson declared that the idea of Hitler "simply" invading Poland is "a lie," and that Germany had "large parts" of territory, including parts of Prussia, that had been “cut off.” He added that the United Kingdom “had nothing to do” with the Treaty of Versailles.

Rees-Mogg's Corrections on the Treaty of Versailles

Rees-Mogg responded that the United Kingdom was, in fact, one of the main conveners and signatories of the Treaty of Versailles, negotiated by Prime Minister David Lloyd George. He also highlighted that the demarcation line between Poland and Russia, known as the Curzon Line, was named after British Secretary of State Lord Curzon.

British Involvement in Guaranteeing Poland

According to Rees-Mogg's correction, the United Kingdom guaranteed Poland's integrity on March 31, 1939, demonstrating direct involvement before the German invasion.

Context of Carlson's Statements on World War II

Carlson's remarks fit a pattern of revisionism that, according to the source UnHerd, includes interviews with figures like Darryl Cooper and Nick Fuentes, who also question Winston Churchill's role and praise Hitler. The narrative attempts to shift blame for the war to figures like Churchill and Franklin Roosevelt, presenting Hitler as a misunderstood leader.

Carlson's Reaction to War Criticism

When confronted with the extent of Hitler's territorial ambitions – which included the occupation of Bohemia and Moravia in 1939, as well as invasions of Denmark, Norway, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg – Carlson did not acknowledge that such actions went beyond merely reversing the Treaty of Versailles.

Implications of the Debate for the Brazilian Public

The episode highlights how revisionist narratives can circulate in international media, influencing perceptions of fundamental historical events. Rees-Mogg's correction demonstrates the importance of confronting inaccurate information with documented facts.

With information from UnHerd, The Telegraph.
